_comment: Single source of truth for CI-plane secret rotation (scripts/rotate_secret.py) AND the App-credential distribution (scripts/distribute_app_secrets.py). Each entry is one rotatable secret and lists every place its value lives: GitHub Actions ENVIRONMENT secrets (github_env_secrets: repo + environment + secret_name), GitHub Actions REPOSITORY secrets (github_repo_secrets: repo + secret_name — the store CI reads when a job declares no 'environment:', e.g. the reusable ci-python-*.yml SDK install; a value written only to environments is invisible to those CI jobs), and/or non-Terraform Vercel project env vars (project_id + env_key). 'retired_github_env_secrets' (repo + environment + secret_name) lists env-level copies a secret has MIGRATED AWAY from (now repo-level): the engine DELETEs each on rotation because a leftover env secret shadows the repo value (env wins over repo). Deletes are idempotent (a 404 is success), and for generate secrets the old token is revoked only after every shadow is gone. SCOPE: CI-plane credentials ONLY (build/deploy plumbing). App secrets in Terraform's SECRETS_INVENTORY (DB URLs, RSA keypair, KDF_SERVICE_KEY, STRIPE_*, OIDC client secrets, CRON_SECRET, etc.) are Terraform-owned — do NOT add them here; a direct write would drift. If one is ever added, set "terraform_managed": true and the engine refuses to write it and points to the terraform SECRETS_ROTATION runbook. 'kind' is the intended primary mode (paste|generate|manual|distribute); 'generator' picks the generate strategy (vercel_token|random_urlsafe); 'per_env' makes generate mint a distinct value per environment; 'shared': true on a vercel_token entry mints ONE token (entry-level 'vercel_token_name') and writes the same value to every target (app/env filters ignored). 'distribute_source_env' opts an entry into distribute_app_secrets.py (ops:distribute-app-secrets): the value is read from that env var (wired by the ops workflow from THIS repo's same-named secret) and fanned out to the entry's github_repo_secrets — the target list doubles as the org-move cleanup checklist for the per-repo copies; 'value_format' (numeric|pem) is its pre-write shape check. 'staging' (D-099) lists a 'paste' entry's staging slots in cicd's ops environment, each { slot, environment }, one slot for an entry held in repository secrets alone and one per environment for an entry held in environments, so a slot's name alone decides where its value goes; Ops · Distribute staged secrets pastes the slots the owner selects and deletes each once its targets are written, and only a 'paste' entry takes a pasted value. A Vercel target marked 'inactive' is left unwritten and named as such, and an active Vercel target whose project_id starts with 'TODO' stops a paste before any write.

secrets.name: GH_PACKAGES_PAT
secrets.description: Fine-grained PAT (contents:read over the owner's repos — at minimum the private package repos kriegerdataforge-sdk + kriegerdataforge-reports-sdk + kriegerdataforge-fmt; ADDING A NEW PRIVATE PACKAGE REPO means BOTH granting it on the token AND adding its consumers below) used at build time to pip-install the private packages (kdf_sdk, kdf_reports, kdf-fmt). GitHub cannot mint PATs via API, so this is paste-only: the owner makes it with a 33-day expiry on the 1st of each month, stages it in its slot GH_PACKAGES_PAT_NEW in cicd's ops, and runs Ops · Distribute staged secrets (D-099), which records its expiry as EXPIRY_GH_PACKAGES_PAT from the token itself. check.expiry below is no longer read. There is ONE global PAT, so it lives ONLY as a REPOSITORY-level Actions secret (github_repo_secrets) — which every job can read, including CI jobs that declare no 'environment:' (the reusable ci-python-*.yml SDK install) AND CD jobs (a job with an environment reads repo + env secrets together). It is deliberately NOT stored per-environment: a same-named env secret would SHADOW the repo value (env wins). The former per-environment copies were already deleted in the one-time repo-level migration, so this token no longer carries retired_github_env_secrets (nothing left to reap). All eight package-consuming repos (kriegerdataforge, fitness-app-backend, tiffanys-space-backend, the scaffold kriegerdataforge-template-fastapi, kriegerdataforge-reports-sdk — whose own CI installs kdf_sdk as a peer dep — plus the kdf-fmt style-lane consumers kriegerdataforge-template-python-package, kriegerdataforge-sdk, and kriegerdataforge-cicd itself) install via this repo-level secret. LESSON (2026-07-17): template-python-package was missing from this list, so the July-1 rotation left it holding a revoked token that failed with 'Invalid username or token' the day it became a consumer — every repo adopting the kdf-fmt style lane must appear here. Since epic W2.5 the ci-python-* lanes prefer a short-lived App installation token when the caller opted in (USE_GITHUB_APP) — this PAT remains the fallback + the local-dev/Vercel-build credential. (Vercel project env vars below are a separate build-time store and are left as-is.)

secrets.name: GH_NPM_TOKEN
secrets.description: CLASSIC PAT with ONLY the read:packages scope, used to install the private GH-Packages npm packages (@needless2say/report-form — @kriegerdataforge/* after the org move). It exists because GitHub Packages accepts ONLY classic PATs or the Actions GITHUB_TOKEN: fine-grained PATs are rejected, so GH_PACKAGES_PAT (fine-grained) can never serve npm, and GitHub Apps have no Packages permission at all (reports-ecosystem epic W3 spike, docs-verified 2026-07). One global value, stored as a REPOSITORY-level Actions secret on the frontend consumer repos (the ci-nextjs-*/cd-nextjs-vercel lanes export it for `npm ci`; a consumer's committed .npmrc interpolates ${GH_NPM_TOKEN}) and as a Vercel project env var on the frontend projects (build-time). Its Vercel entries below are marked inactive until their project ids are filled, so a paste names them as left unwritten and never as written, and the owner sets those four by hand meanwhile; a TODO id on an active entry stops a paste before any write. Where possible prefer the ZERO-secret alternative for consumer CI: a per-repo Actions-access grant on the package (see the npm template's PRIVATE_GH_PACKAGES guide). GitHub cannot mint PATs via API, so this is paste-only: the owner makes it with a 33-day expiry on the 1st of each month, stages it in its slot GH_NPM_TOKEN_NEW in cicd's ops, and runs Ops · Distribute staged secrets (D-099), which records its expiry as EXPIRY_GH_NPM_TOKEN from the token itself. Recipe: the owner's SECRET_ROTATION.md (kriegerdataforge-context/ops/) §8.2a.

secrets.name: VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN
secrets.description: ONE shared, account-scoped Vercel token used EVERYWHERE: every app repo's CI/CD deploys with it AND the terraform repo uses it to MANAGE Vercel (create projects, set env vars) via the Terraform provider. Consolidated 2026-06-30 from the former split (VERCEL_TOKEN deploy + VERCEL_API_TOKEN terraform) — both were the same Full-Account-privilege token, so two separate tokens was pure redundancy. Because there is ONE value everywhere it is stored ONLY as a REPOSITORY-level secret per repo (github_repo_secrets), NOT per-environment: a same-named env secret would SHADOW the repo value (env wins over repo), so the former prod/dev env copies are listed under retired_github_env_secrets and DELETED on rotation. CD jobs keep 'environment:' for their OTHER per-env secrets (VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, DB URLs, keys) and read this token from repo-level in the same job. Auto-minted via the Vercel API as a single token, written to every repo target; the previous token is revoked only if ALL writes succeed AND every retired env shadow was removed (otherwise both stay valid so no repo holds a revoked token). App/env filters are ignored — it is one value everywhere. In the terraform repo this secret feeds TF_VAR_vercel_api_token (the provider's variable name is unchanged). Its expiry is RECORDED, not hand kept: the rotation's ops run reads the earliest expiry among the live tokens of its name through the master token, after each mint and on a record-expiry dispatch, and keeps it as the cicd repository variable EXPIRY_VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN, which the weekly monitor reads, so the monitor doubles as a watchdog if the rotation ever stops. check.expiry below is no longer read.

secrets.name: CICD_PAT
secrets.description: Fine-grained PAT carrying the full provisioning/fallback scope: Repository Administration + Contents + Environments + Secrets + Variables + Actions + Issues + Pull requests (all read/write) over ALL repos (incl. future), plus Metadata read. The rotation + kit workflows mint ephemeral GitHub App tokens (docs/design/github-app-migration.md) and use CICD_PAT only as the `|| secrets.CICD_PAT` fallback; its sole ACTIVE consumer is issue-create-repo.yml (creating a personal-account repo needs a user PAT — an App token can't, until the org move). GitHub has no PAT-creation API, so it is rotated BY HAND — monitored only (no engine targets). Retirement is tracked in the central roadmap (KDF docs/engineering/GITHUB_FUTURE_ENHANCEMENTS.md, Enhancement 1). Recipe: the owner's SECRET_ROTATION.md (kriegerdataforge-context/ops/) §8.3. Last rotated 2026-06-30 with a 30-day token. It lives in cicd's ops environment alone (the secrets fence), so the weekly monitor cannot read it, and its expiry is RECORDED by the rotation's ops run as the cicd repository variable EXPIRY_CICD_PAT, which the monitor reads. check.expiry below is no longer read.

secrets.name: VERCEL_MASTER_TOKEN
secrets.description: Full-Account Vercel token the engine uses to mint/delete the shared deploy/management token (VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN). Stays MANUAL (paste-only): minting requires Full Account scope, and this is the bootstrap credential the rotation itself depends on — it can't rotate itself with itself. Rotate it by hand before expiry (recipe §8.4), straight into cicd's ops environment, and prove it with the rotation's prove-master dispatch. Monitored only (no engine targets). Last rotated 2026-06-30 with a 30-day Vercel token. It lives in ops alone (the secrets fence), so its expiry is RECORDED by the rotation's ops run as the cicd repository variable EXPIRY_VERCEL_MASTER_TOKEN, which the weekly monitor reads. check.expiry below is no longer read.

secrets.name: KDF_APP_ID
secrets.description: The read only GitHub App's numeric id, Contents and Metadata read alone, installed on the repos the code reads (the secrets fence). Not sensitive by itself, but stored as a secret beside KDF_APP_PRIVATE_KEY so the pair travels together. Each repo that runs a lane holds its own copy under this name, since a personal account cannot share secrets: the run-e2e mint, the ci-python-* private package installs, the SDK's Merge Gate and cicd's own positive control. Every mint from it asks for reads alone. Fanned out by scripts/distribute_app_secrets.py through the ops:distribute-app-secrets issue flow from its source, KDF_READER_APP_ID in cicd's ops environment, so no key is pasted from a file. The writing App's pair is KDF_WRITER_APP_ID and KDF_WRITER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY in ops alone, never a repository secret. The target list below is the inventory of every repo holding a copy. The id never rotates, only the key, so there is no check block.

secrets.name: KDF_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
secrets.description: Private key (.pem) of the read only GitHub App, beside KDF_APP_ID, the pair always travelling together over the same list of repos. Every lane mints a read token from it. It has no expiry, but rotate it periodically, since GitHub Apps hold several keys for a rotation with no downtime. The source is KDF_READER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY in cicd's ops environment, made there from the App's settings and never kept on a drive, and ops:distribute-app-secrets fans it out with KDF_APP_ID, both values per repo before the next. After a new key, run that flow, or the copies keep minting from the old key and break once it is deleted. Recipe: the owner's SECRET_ROTATION.md (kriegerdataforge-context/ops/) §8.3a.

secrets.name: REPORTS_CRON_SECRET_FITNESS_APP
secrets.description: cicd-side COPY of the fitness backend's REPORTS_CRON_SECRET — the X-Cron-Secret value the reports-triage trigger (trigger-reports-triage.yml / ops:triage-reports, targets in scripts/reports_registry.json) sends to POST /reports/triage/cron. DUAL-STORE: the AUTHORITATIVE value is Terraform app-side (fitness module reports_cron_secret tfvars); rotate there FIRST, then stage the same value in the slot of each environment it serves and distribute (SECRET_ROTATION.md §8.13a, D-099). High-entropy opaque string (openssl rand -hex 32), no expiry to track. Until this copy is set, the trigger engine fails closed before any POST; until the app-side value is set, the endpoint itself answers 503 (PL-056 fail-closed). It lives in cicd's dev and prod environments, a copy in each, the reports workflows reading it in the environment they run in, and a paste writes the one environment it names, so the same value is pasted once for each.

secrets.name: REPORTS_CRON_SECRET_TIFFANYS_SPACE
secrets.description: cicd-side COPY of the tiffanys backend's REPORTS_CRON_SECRET — the X-Cron-Secret value the reports-triage trigger (trigger-reports-triage.yml / ops:triage-reports, targets in scripts/reports_registry.json) sends to POST /reports/triage/cron. DUAL-STORE: the AUTHORITATIVE value is Terraform app-side (tiffanys-space module reports_cron_secret tfvars); rotate there FIRST, then stage the same value in the slot of each environment it serves and distribute (SECRET_ROTATION.md §8.13a, D-099). High-entropy opaque string (openssl rand -hex 32), no expiry to track. Until this copy is set, the trigger engine fails closed before any POST; until the app-side value is set, the endpoint itself answers 503 (PL-056 fail-closed). It lives in cicd's dev and prod environments, a copy in each, the reports workflows reading it in the environment they run in, and a paste writes the one environment it names, so the same value is pasted once for each.

secrets.name: KDF_HUB_URL_DEV
secrets.description: cicd-side copy of the auth hub's DEV base URL, which hub-prune-tokens.yml POSTs its prune route on. A secret because this public repository does not publish the hub's address. One entry per value, so a paste writes the DEV value alone and never the PROD one. It lives in cicd's dev environment as KDF_HUB_URL, the name the prune reads in the environment it runs in.

secrets.name: KDF_HUB_URL_PROD
secrets.description: cicd-side copy of the auth hub's PROD base URL, which hub-prune-tokens.yml POSTs its prune route on. A secret because this public repository does not publish the hub's address. One entry per value, so a paste writes the PROD value alone and never the DEV one. It lives in cicd's prod environment as KDF_HUB_URL, the name the prune reads in the environment it runs in.

secrets.name: KDF_HUB_CRON_SECRET_DEV
secrets.description: cicd-side COPY of the auth hub's DEV CRON_SECRET, the bearer hub-prune-tokens.yml sends to the prune route. The authoritative value is Terraform's on the hub's DEV project, so rotate it there first, then paste the same value here. One entry per value, so a paste writes the DEV value alone. It lives in cicd's dev environment as KDF_HUB_CRON_SECRET, the name the prune reads in the environment it runs in.

secrets.description: cicd-side COPY of the auth hub's PROD CRON_SECRET, the bearer hub-prune-tokens.yml sends to the prune route. The authoritative value is Terraform's on the hub's PROD project, so rotate it there first, then paste the same value here. One entry per value, so a paste writes the PROD value alone. It lives in cicd's prod environment as KDF_HUB_CRON_SECRET, the name the prune reads in the environment it runs in.
